question.text: Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(\dfrac13\right),$ calculate $P\left(X \leq 2\right).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.explanation:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda$ has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \lambda e^{-\lambda x}, & x \geq 0 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

We're given that

\[ X\sim \textrm{Exp} \left( \dfrac13 \right). \]

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases}\dfrac13e^{-x/3}, & x \geq 0 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]Therefore, we can calculate $P\left(X \leq 2\right)$ as follows:

\[\begin{align*} P\left(X \leq 2\right) &= \int_0^{2} f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^{2} \dfrac13 e^{-x/3} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= -\left. e^{-x/3}\right|_0^{2} \\[5pt] &= -e^{-2/3} + e^0 \\[5pt] &\approx 0.4866 \end{align*}\]

question.text: Given that the random variable $W\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(0.25\right),$ calculate $P\left(1 \leq W \leq 5\right).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.explanation:
An exponential random variable $W$ with rate $\lambda$ has the following probability density function:

\[ f(w) = \begin{cases} \lambda e^{-\lambda w}, & w \geq 0 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

We're given that

\[ W\sim \textrm{Exp} \left( 0.25 \right). \]

So, $W$ has the following probability density function:

\[ f(w) = \begin{cases}0.25e^{-0.25w}, & w \geq 0 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]Therefore, we can calculate $P\left(1 \leq W \leq 5\right)$ as follows:

\[\begin{align*} P\left(1 \leq W \leq 5\right) &= \int_1^{5} f(w) \, \textrm dw \\[5pt] &= \int_1^{5} 0.25 e^{-0.25w} \, \textrm dw \\[5pt] &= -e^{-0.25w}\Big\lvert_1^{5} \\[5pt] &= -e^{-1.25} + e^{-0.25}\\[5pt] &\approx 0.4923 \end{align*}\]

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating Probabilities Using the Memoryless Property

question.text: Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(\dfrac 25\right),$ calculate $P\left(X > 7 \,\big|\, X > 2\right).$
question.explanation:
Given a random variable $X \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\lambda),$ and two positive real numbers $s, t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that \[ P(X>s+t \, \big|\, X>s) = P(X > t) = e^{-\lambda t}. \]

In our case, we have $\lambda = \dfrac25,$ $s=2,$ and $s+t=7.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows: \[ t = (t+s) - s = 7-2 = 5 \]

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get \begin{align*} P\left(X > 7 \,\big|\, X > 2\right) &= e^{-\lambda t} \\[5pt] & = e^{-(2/5) \cdot (5)} \\[5pt] &= e^{-2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1{e^2}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(\dfrac 12\right),$ calculate $P\left(X > 3 \,\big|\, X > 1\right).$
question.explanation:
Given a random variable $X \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\lambda),$ and two positive real numbers $s, t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that \[ P(X>s+t \, \big|\, X>s) = P(X > t) = e^{-\lambda t}. \]

In our case, we have $\lambda = 2,$ $s=1,$ and $s+t=3.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows: \[ t = (t+s) - s = 3-1 = 2 \]

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get \begin{align*} P\left(X > 3 \,\big|\, X > 1\right) &= e^{-\lambda t} \\[5pt] & = e^{-(1/2) \cdot (2)} \\[5pt] &= e^{-1}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1e. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(5\right),$ calculate $P\left(X \leq 6 \, \big |\, X > 4\right).$
question.explanation:
Given a random variable $X \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\lambda),$ and two positive real numbers $s, t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that \[ P(X>s+t \, \big |\, X>s) = P(X > t) = e^{-\lambda t}. \]

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows: \[ P(X\leq s+t \, \big|\, X>s) = 1-P(X>s+t \, \big |\, X>s) = 1-e^{-\lambda t} \]

In our case, we have $\lambda = 5,$ $s=4,$ and $s+t=6.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows: \[ t = (t+s) - s = 6 - 4 = 2 \]

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get \begin{align*} P\left(X \leq 6 \, \big |\, X > 4\right) &= 1-e^{-\lambda t} \\[5pt] & = 1-e^{-(5) \cdot (2)} \\[5pt] &= 1-e^{-10}\\[5pt] \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(3\right),$ calculate $P\left(X \leq \dfrac 13 \, \bigg |\, X > \dfrac 14\right).$
question.explanation:
Given a random variable $X \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\lambda),$ and two positive real numbers $s, t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that \[ P(X>s+t \, \big |\, X>s) = P(X > t) = e^{-\lambda t}. \]

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows: \[ P(X\leq s+t \, \big|\, X>s) = 1-P(X>s+t \, \big |\, X>s) = 1-e^{-\lambda t} \]

In our case, we have $\lambda = 3,$ $s=\dfrac 14,$ and $s+t=\dfrac 13.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows: \[ t = (t+s) - s = \dfrac 13 - \dfrac 14 = \dfrac{1}{12} \]

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get \begin{align*} P\left(X \leq \dfrac 13 \, \bigg |\, X > \dfrac 14\right) &= 1-e^{-\lambda t} \\[5pt] & = 1-e^{-(3) \cdot (1/12)} \\[5pt] &= 1-e^{-1/4}\\[5pt] \end{align*}
